bull.b: The Phase 2 results provide evidence that PGN-EDODM1 may affect both the underlying molecular defect and several functional manifestations of DM1. If replicated in larger cohorts, this could strengthen the program’s clinical differentiation and support future regulatory progress.

A cash position described as sufficient to fund operations into 2028 gives PepGen time to generate additional clinical data without relying immediately on repeated financing. That runway can support execution through later-stage development milestones and reduce near-term operational disruption.

Modest and declining debt gives PepGen a comparatively manageable capital structure for a clinical-stage biotechnology company. Lower leverage reduces fixed financial obligations and preserves more flexibility to direct available capital toward clinical development and other strategic priorities.

bear.b: PepGen has not yet established commercial revenue and continues to consume substantial cash while funding development activities. This makes future progress dependent on clinical execution and access to external capital, leaving the business financially exposed if timelines extend.

The partial clinical hold remains a material regulatory obstacle because it can constrain development of FREEDOM2 and delay the path toward an end-of-Phase 2 meeting. Even with encouraging data, unresolved regulatory requirements could extend timelines and increase development costs.

bear.t: Equity Base Erosion And Financing Need
bear.b: Persistent losses have reduced the equity base, while the proposed share offering shows that continued development requires substantial external funding. Additional equity financing can support the pipeline, but it also signals ongoing capital dependence and may dilute existing ownership.
